notes.title: v0.2 Hotfix
notes.content:
[p][b]1.)[/b] v0.2 proved to be pretty incompatible with a couple of mods, specifically ones that added spells or skills to your hotbar that didn't otherwise exist in the game. The result was some failed file loads, and lost skills / items / spells, etc. 

I've added some checks in the game's code to help prevent data loss issues for players, but the mods will likely still not work. [/p][p][/p][p][b]2.)[/b] Previously, SimPlayers needed to zone or leave a group to acquire new spells. This worked fine on Stowaway's Step because by design players were zoning in and out of the tomb. 

Willowwatch offers a different play area, which encourages players to remain in the zone for an extended time meaning SimPlayers were not refreshing their spell lists at all.

SimPlayers now have gotten better at planning, and they've pre-bought their spells so when they level up they'll have them at their disposal immediately. [/p][p][/p][p][b]3.)[/b] Fixed some UI issues as reported. 

Thank you for your patience!
Brian [/p]

notes.title: Erenshor: 2025 Development Roadmap Update
notes.content: [p][b][u]Hello Erenshor community![/u][/b] [/p][p]Erenshor launched almost 2.5 months ago, and from day 1 the community has been providing feedback and ideas for the game's future. I believe I've read just about every single message that has come my way and there have been some pretty consistent themes in there. [/p][p][u]Some recurring themes:[/u][/p][list][*][p]The game plays too fast[/p][/*][*][p]The combat is unclear and hard to read[/p][/*][*][p]The endgame gets too easy[/p][/*][*][p]The middle game gets too hard[/p][/*][*][p]We want an Archer / Bard / Summoner / Buff class etc.[/p][/*][*][p]WHERE ARE RAIDS??[/p][/*][/list][p]Using that info, and aligning it with my own vision for the game, I've come up with a development plan for the rest of 2025. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/866467dadb46d7064d2b451aeef1bd28c872a1c4.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Increased Party Size: [/b]Erenshor players may notice that the game expects certain party roles to be fulfilled: DPS, Heals, Crowd Control, and Tanking. Limiting the party to 4 characters prevents players from expanding on one of these roles to fit their playstyle. You can't bring two healers without sacrificing something else. You can't stack DPS without losing CC or Heals. etc. Adding an extra party slot will allow players to customize their builds more, without punishing themselves.[/p][p]It goes without saying that this will also require a [b]full game rebalance[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Smoother Combat Flow: [/b]One player put it best to me: Combat in Erenshor just comes down to "Can you out-heal the NPC damage". This stems from:[/p][list][*][p]Mana is 'unlimited' right now with duelist mana restore spells. Mana pool doesn't matter. I plan to address this by removing the duelist mana restoration spell line completely. In-combat mana regeneration will be reduced greatly, and out of combat mana regeneration will be increased greatly. [b]The size of your manapool will matter.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Spell mana costs and SimPlayer spell usage will be tweaked to support this change. An able party should be able to complete encounters without running out of mana through careful mana management.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing spells heal for too much right now. You can plan on the max level heal spell 'fully healing' just about any player in the game once you get it. Heal spells will shift to faster cast, lower amounts. You'll be able to decide to top up the tank right now, or wait until he's lower and hit him then. [/p][/*][*][p]Damage is too spiky. Currently, NPCs hit for huge amounts of damage, and can "2-round" a tank in some cases. That's not fun, that's hoping RNG is kind to you. I want to stretch combat out - NPCs will hit for less, but they'll hit at a quicker pace. You'll be able to predict incoming damage and plan your stategy around that. [/p][/*][*][p]NPCs will be getting cast bars so players can plan to interrupt spells. Damage spells longer casting time will help facilitate this. [/p][/*][*][p]MOBs die too fast in many cases (not all cases). With the addition of a 5th party member, their HP pools will need an increase. [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Itemization: [/b]Anyone who has played to endgame knows that getting blessed items and ascending them to "purple" is the be-all-end-all of class gearing. Purple items use a formula that adds value to [b]every stat[/b] on an item. This ends up making a very select few items BIS for every class. [/p][p]In this update, purple items will only enhance stats that already exist on items. So your DPS ring will be better at DPS. Your tanky armor will be better at being tanky. You'll be able to pick and choose which items you want to ascend based on your playstyle. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Zone Reworks: [/b]The dungeons of Erenshor will be expanded in many cases to allow for new named mobs, items, and exploration. Some earlier dungeons (Island Tomb, Krakengard) will need full rebuilds. They're crowded with a party of 4, and 5 will be worse. Expect some renovations. [/p][p][/p][p][b]During this combat rework this summer, patches will be far less frequent than they've been since launch. [/b]This is the first huge content patch Erenshor is receiving, and the game build will not be in a state where I can quickly patch and fix things for the duration of this work. [/p][p][/p][p][b]The Goal of these reworks is to set the stage for raids: [/b]I want to have Erenshor's first raid live by the end of this year. It's really important to me that I start developing raids from a good starting point of game balance. [/p][p][/p][p][b]I worked for a long time to make all my items purple and now they're being nerfed? [/b]TL;DR; Yes, many will be 'less good' than they are now. I understand players have put in a lot of hours to get their characters to build completion and the new purple items may no longer be your BIS. There will be dev commands in game to add Planar Stones and Sivakruxes to your inventory to ascend new items. If you feel that you don't want to do the grind again to get your characters to BIS, I will share those dev commands with you. [b]It's a single player game, we can do things like that[/b] :) [/p]

notes.title: 6/16/25 - Erenshor Server Admin Menu (balance options)
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Erenshor Players![/h2][p][/p][p][b]Since day 1, one specific question has rang throughout this community: [/b]"Where are my quest markers and my map?"[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/38731ca330423b4a8ad19a6172fd75fce78cac7d.png"][/img][/p][p] The goal of Erenshor has always been to pay homage to EverQuest and the "old ways", but it has become more and more apparent that folks who really want to enjoy solo MMORPG gameplay are bouncing off the game due to the lack of guidance (and a huge portion of players were using the minimap mod and quest helper mod.) [/p][p]Erenshor first and foremost is an "MMORPG experience that respects your time." I've always been steadfast on "you bought the game, play however you want" and in that spirit, I've left save files unencrypted and the curious user may uncover some Developer Commands in the game too.   [/p][p]Now, in addition to that, I've introduced a new options menu:  [b]"The Server Admin Panel"[/b][/p][p]In this options menu, accessible only from the login screen you can adjust the following game settings to your liking:[/p][list][*][p]Minimap[/p][/*][*][p]Quest Markers[/p][/*][*][p]Server XP rate[/p][/*][*][p]Server NPC HP scaling[/p][/*][*][p]Server NPC Damage Scaling[/p][/*][*][p]Server Rare Loot drop rate
[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/de1fb52ae63e086d4aacf8f425bf91ca733343d4.png"][/img][/p][p]There are pre-set configurations to choose from as well:[/p][list][*][p]Recommended: No map, no quest markers, 1x to all scaling options[/p][/*][*][p]Challenge: No map, no quest markers, [b]1x[/b] XP, [b]2x[/b] NPC HP, [b]1.5x[/b] NPC Damage, [b]1x[/b] Loot rate[/p][/*][*][p]Causal: Map enabled, Quest Markers enabled, [b]1.5x[/b] XP, [b]1x[/b] NPC HP, [b]1x[/b] NPC Damage, [b]1.5x[/b] Loot rate[/p][/*][*][p]Extended: Map enabled, no quest markers, [b].5x[/b] XP modifier, [b]2.5x[/b] NPC HP modifer, [b]1x[/b] NPC Damage modifier, [b].8x[/b] Loot drop rate[/p][/*][/list][p]You can adjust the difficulty as much as you want, including up to [b]5x[/b] NPC HP, [b]5x[/b] NPC Damage (lol you'll die), [b]5x[/b] XP gain, and [b]5x[/b] Loot rate. 

[b]The game will [u]always[/u] be balanced around the RECOMMENDED settings.
[/b][/p][p]Welcome to Erenshor, all gamers: enjoy the new toys.[/p][p]-Brian [/p][p](PS - as with all major changes, please keep an eye out for bugs and I'll squash 'em immediately)

notes.title: 6/3/25 - The Blight gets Blightier, and other changes
notes.content:
Hey folks, some new changes for this evening! 

[list]
[*] Rewrote tab-targeting:
   a.) will grab nearest target if nothing is targeted or current target is not in range
   b.) will grab next nearest target if something in range is currently targeted
   c.) shift+tab will cycle backwards furthest to nearest
 
[*] Spectrum now triggers auto attack ON if that setting is enabled
[*] Spells can now be interrupted instantly with strafe keys 
[*] Block and Dodge Books now list appropriate classes
[*] SimPlayers won't ask to buy Planar Stones or Sivakruxes anymore because they no longer pay up for those items
[*] Added an "Assist MA" hotkey in the group roles window. Using this (Shift + 2) will automatically set you on the Main Assist's target
[*] Buffed Sivakayan Tricorner (more dex, more res, more cha)
[*] Added a new enemy in the blight. 
[*] Large wandering enemies make idle sound cues now so you can hear them coming. This has NOTHING to do with the blight enemy at all. Trust me. 
[*] Buffed Paladin Astra Weapon -- Paladins are the only class who's Astra weapon is arguably not their BIS. 
[/list]

That does it for this update, see ya next time! 

-B

notes.title: 5/31/25 - Friendlist Fix, Jaws Bug Fix, and a Vendor at Ripper's Keep
notes.content:
Just a few fixes and tweaks to be had today:

[list]
[*] DEBUG FIX: Players using the first Character Slot will notice they have a lot of 'surprise friends'. This is a result of SimPlayers being generated with a default "FriendedBy" value of 0 instead of -1. (0 correlates to that first slot). 

You're welcome to keep all your surprise friends, but if you'd like a fresh friends list, there's a debug button that appears when viewing friends. This will reset any SimPlayer with a FriendedBy=0 to FriendedBy=-1 like they should be. This will include friends you've intentionally added, so you will have to re-add friends after applying this fix.

Today's patch fixes this initial bug as well, so folks who purchased the game on or after 5/31 need not worry about this issue. 

[*] Siraethe in Jaws of Sivakaya was not autoattacking due to a script issue. She's fixed, and much meaner. 
[*] Ripper's Keep now has a vendor

[/list]

That does it for this update, see ya next time! 

-B

[b]IMPORTANT: DODGE AND BLOCK SKILL HAVE CHANGED[/b] -- you will need to go to Port Azure to buy your upgraded versions. 

The goal of this patch was to establish Paladin's identities more clearly:
[list]
[*]The Tank Paladin: Using sword and shield, Paladins receive mitigation bonuses and rely less on dodge and block. This should lead to more predictable damage rates, having the Paladin be more likely to be 'chipped down' instead of either mitigating everything via Dodge or Block, or taking a big hit. 
[*]The DPS Paladin: Using a 2H Weapon, Paladins forfeit their mitigation bonuses, but gain a 2x attack damage modifier and some new skills. While 2H Paladins may find it harder to tank on-tier content, they'll compliment certain group structures quite well.
[/list]

Additionally, other classes were dodging and blocking TOO much. By splitting Dodge and Block into different levels, I was able to limit how effective the skills are for non-paladin classes, This will keep Dodge and Block as a "bonus mitigation chance" and not a reliable way to off tank. 

Feedback is welcome (and wanted) on these changes.

[*] While using a shield, Paladins will gain a 2x bonus to all armor mitigations
[*] When not using a shield, Paladins will have no armor bonuses

[*] With the tank changes, higher end content should be easier overall and the feeling of need for "purple" items should be reduced. 
[/list]

notes.title: (Almost) One Month In! Upcoming focus on getting the balance right
notes.content:
Hey folks! It's been just about a month since Erenshor launched and honestly it still doesn't feel real. To date, Erenshor has received over 800 "Very Positive" reviews - which indie games live and die by, and honestly I can't even express how incredible this has all been. 

Updates have been slow this past week as I've been at PAX and got to meet a ton of you guys which was super cool - we have an incredible community here, and that holds true in person too.

I've spent a lot of time looking at some achievement analytics, watching streamers play, reading comments on the forums, and I thought that laying out a little 'short term roadmap' would be a good way to start diving back into the project now that PAX is over. So, without further delay, and balance is on my mind in a lot of areas.

So far, I think we've had a win with community feedback leading to XP changes across all levels including boss XP bonuses - let's keep this two-way communication going, but to do that, I have to be open about my own ideas and so that's the point of this post. 

And because balance is a tough subject in any game (especially if it means reductions in some areas) I feel like transparency is key, so here's a bit of a stream-of-thought post on what I'm looking into first: 

[h2]Class Changes[/h2]
[b]DRUID[/b]
Druids have already had a few changes: Fixes to their Heal-Over-Time spells, the addition of a higher damage spell line, and reductions to resistances on their DOT spells. There has also been some stat scaling changes over the past month. In addition to that, druids desperately need better pet summons to compete with some found items in the game.

Druids have also had some reductions to some ascension skills, their vengeful healing skill has had its proc probability reduced slightly, and it will likely be further adjusted in the near future. The reason for this is that previously, druids could simply spam-heal a target and do massive damage to their target's target. This wasn't a fun or dynamic playstyle and it encouraged druids to just spam-heal and do nothing else. Not the dynamic I was after.

Overall, druids are in a far better spot since launch, but there's room to improve. 

[b]DUELISTS[/b]
Duelists are in a relatively good place right now. Their backstab skills are scaling well at level, their DPS numbers are pretty solid, and they have a lot of survivability options. Backstab has a wide range of possible damage, which I personally was aiming for, making those BIG hits feel good.

Early on Duelists had some DPS reductions as their backstab formula was changed and their offhand weapons were made to respect weapon delay. 

Duelists also have some scaling issues vs high level targets where level difference is overriding stats, meaning a duelist with 800 dexterity and a duelist with 400 dexterity will do around the same DPS, which is not intended and needs addressing - but this is true for all classes. 

One thing I've heard said repeatedly is that Duelists need more 'class exclusive weapons' and I agree. Itemization will change, and likely new level 1-35 content will come throughout early access and I'll explore some fun new toys for them there. 

[b]ARCANIST[/b]
I honestly love where Arcanists are at. I think they're the best-balanaced class at the moment and are just about where I want them to be. 

Arcanists need some tools to deal with large pulls, such as some potential utility spells. Top of mind is an AE stun spell to allow Arcanists to control a situation involving large pulls, and some avenues to quickly reset their cooldowns in order to give the spell rotation some flare. 

I'd also like to introduce some charm options for Arcanists that tie procs into their spells, such as a small chance to stun on any cast, or a small chance to lifesteal or mana steal on any cast.

Speaking of Mana, Arcanists need a method to restore their own mana since that responsibility was handed to duelists. I'm not sure exactly how this will look yet, whether its a consumable item or an ability. 

Some early changes to resist scaling has ensured they are strong on the DPS charts, and while SimPlayer arcanists need some help learning their spell rotations, I think in the hands of a good player, Arcanists are absolutely lethal. 

[b]PALADINS[/b]
Paladins are very overpowered at the moment. At max level / max ascension they often sit near the top of DPS charts while also being monstrously tanky. 

I want to find a way to give paladins some options, including allowing for DPS-focused builds around 2-handed weapons at the expense of their tanking ability. Introducing more 2H-focused skills is a priority for Paladins, in order to give them the option to be DPS-focused for XP grinding while having the option to switch to tank-mode for bosses. 

Some of their ascension skills may need to be scaled down slightly to bring them in-line with where their maxed-out DPS should be, but the goal is not to gut them, its to allow the player to consciously switch modes while leaving both modes intact - just not simultaneously. 

[b]SKILLS[/b]
There are some problems with skills - specifically BLOCK and DODGE. 

Block and Dodge both are a 100% mitigation skill from the moment you get it, and it doesn't matter if your attacker is 3 levels below you or 20 ahead of you, you can mitigate entire hits just by having the skill at no cost to anything else. The only requirement is that the target is in front of you.

Currently, it's more efficient to pull 6-7 mobs on your paladin and leave arcanists / crowd control out of your group and let the paladin's mitigation handle the situation. This isn't ideal, and removes an entire mechanic from the game (crowd control)

Block and Dodge work the same for every class, which is also not optimal. Likely, Block and Dodge will be split into tiers of skill, so you'll find Block I, Block II, Block III, Block IV books, with Paladins being able to use all tiers, and other classes being locked out of the higher tiers of the skill - setting Paladins apart as the ideal tank.

Currently, Block and Dodge leave little room for expansion and makes balancing tricky. I am considering a few potential avenues to fix this in addition to the skill tiers - so far my brainstorming has lead me to some ideas:

[list]
[*]Cooldowns on the abilities - Block and Dodge can only proc so often. This opens up paths for cooldown reduction later on.
[*]Block and / or Dodge work only on the being you have targeted. This makes a Paladin extremely effective at tanking bosses, while still making Arcanists (or other future CC classes) necessary for larger pulls. 
[*]Shields have a % block visible stat on them, so you'll have to decide on your equipment and its effectiveness at blocking. E.g. One shield might block 15% of damage on proc, while another blocks 50%. 
[/list]

[b]ENDGAME BALANCE[/b]
Sivakruxes are a pain point for a lot of folks, I get it. Planar stones are in high supply but you're locked out of upgrades by Sivakruxes. This is admittedly a very incomplete mechanic, and I'm looking at tuning it in more here.

[list]
[*]Sivakruxes will become much more common in the near future through treasure maps - which will also become much more common through a few avenues such as: fishing, rare wandering vendors, and overall loot drop rates.
[*]Planar stones will become exceedingly rare for now. Keep in mind that in 1.0, players will not be soft-stuck at Astra and Demented, they'll be looking to progress into raids. "Purpling" all of your gear prior to those encounters will not be necessary nor the common path for players. You guys are welcome to do it now, for lack of other things to do, but keep this in mind as you do it. 
[*]Raids will introduce more common sources to get Planar Stones (since they'll take place in the planes), and Raid Gear will have its own, alternate upgrade paths as well which will also include Planar Stones. 
[/list]

Keep in mind that by grinding yourself into full purple gear, you may trivialize some early raid content. This won't be a huge deal, but raid content is going to pick up at approximately "Astra" level of difficulty. I don't want you guys to stop playing, but time may be better spent gearing up some other SimPlayers so you have a full raid force ready to go, rather than full-purpling yourself.

Treasure Map balance is still a work in progress in general, and its loot table will increase to make them continuously interesting to do. They are in a very 'placeholder' state for now. 

[b]SIMPLAYERS[/b]
SimPlayers need to be smarter about handling their Aggro. Especially for Druid players who are at the mercy of SimPlayers playing Tank + DPS roles, things can go south very fast. This adjustment is coming.

SimPlayers need to be able to use active items including food. HOWEVER, this will mean that items that summon pets are going to be too strong. Adding 3 more summoned Malaroths to an XP group will cause massive trivialization to many areas, and so it's likely those summons will be reduced in effectiveness, either across the board, or depending on how many are active at once in the area. They will still be fantastic toys to give to your alt characters though. 

SimPlayers are also still occasionally wandering off or falling off of the navmesh and getting stuck. This is a "most wanted bug" at the moment. If you find a reliable method to recreate SimPlayers getting stuck, please DM me in discord - we'll do something fun for the first person who comes up with a reliable method to reproduce this so I can do it in an editing environment and see what's happening exactly. 

[b]OTHER UPCOMING CHANGES:[/b]
Fishing rework or tweaks (possibly making a mini game out of it?)
Auction House Rework
Tiered tools for Fishing and Mining
Getting the first bit of 35+ content in game (end of the quest that leaves you back on Stowaway's Step)


[b]This is not by any means the full plan[/b], or a definite plan. This is where I'm at on brainstorming and I absolutely value community feedback. So let's have a chat. 

Obviously, throughout all of this, I will continue to prioritize bugs and other issues with the game. By getting this balance right now, I can keep the door open for new classes and content - both of which I greatly look forward to adding.

Thank you all for being a part of the Erenshor community!

notes.title: Demo Update - February 2nd, 2025
notes.content:
[h1]Happy February all! [/h1]

As Erenshor continues on its final stretch of development before Early Access, I feel it's important to continue to make sure the demo is an accurate reflection of what's to come. As such, here are the recent additions:

[u][b]Game Play: [/b][/u]
[list]
[*]Screenshake added on player-casted spells. (can be disabled in options)
[*]New particle effects and SFX for nearly all spells
[*]When turning in quest rewards, you can now drag items to the NPC model to add them to the trade window, instead of having to drag each item to the trade window
[*]Player can now cancel a spell cast by moving during the cast
[*]Font size in the chat log can be scaled from the options menu
[*]SimPlayer Arcanists will be better about refilling player mana
[*]Blessed items on vis gear slots will show a mild particle effect in game on the player or SimPlayer model
[/list]

[u][b]Balance / Combat: [/b][/u]
[list]
[*]All NPCs do more damage
[*]Players Block and Dodge only trigger if you're facing your attacker
[*]Any non-tank SimPlayer class will try to position itself behind its melee target. Enemies around level 6+ get passive mitigations such as dodge and block. These abilities will only trigger from attacks coming from their front.
[*]SimPlayers are WAY more proficient at using heal spells
[*]SimPlayer tanks will taunt and try to tank all mobs that are not CC'd
[*]SimPlayers will no longer cast DOT spells on full health mobs. This prevents them DOTing a mob that may need to be mezzed if the group choose to engage another target. They'll begin casting DOTs at 95% life.
[*]SimPlayers will no longer 'stack' different crowd control spells on a mob. One is enough, and they know it now.
[*]SimPlayers will be better at 'assisting' whoever is the group tank. If the player is a tank, and the group contains another paladin, the player will be considered 'main tank'. 
[*]SimPlayer pullers will issue an 'attack' command to the group when they return to camp to ensure idle or distant group members engage the target
[*]Pets and charmed mobs will never attack a dazzled target. They'll engage as soon as a player breaks the dazzle.
[*]SimPlayers will not pull if they're out of mana.
[*]SimPlayer target selection and pulling logic is improved
[*]SimPlayers will now pull targets with a spell if possible, instead of "body pulling"
[*]DOTs can now stack between casters, meaning if two druids both cast the same DOT spell on a target, they will both land and do damage. 
[*]Added bonus and penalty to melee damage roles based on the difference between attacker and its target. Red con mobs are harder, blue con mobs are now easier. 
[*]Added a maximum movespeed debuff, maximum attack speed debuff cap on NPCs. Two druids casting snare will have additional effects, however, they do not stack infinitely
[*]Pullers will only target mobs -4 through +5 levels from themselves
[*]SimPlayers will no longer 'spam' status effects on mobs. Once it's on, they won't continuously refresh it
[/list]

[u][b]Other: [/b][/u]
[list]
[*]Upon exiting the game, a 'backup snapshot' of your game is saved. In the event of data loss due to bad steam cloud syncs or other issues, you can load a local backup from the main menu.
[*]"Reset Simplayer" moved into its own sub-menu on title screen
[*]SimPlayers should be better about choosing equipment to use
[*]Quest turn-ins were sometimes duplicating items, they no longer will
[*]DPS calculation on weapon info cards no longer ignores 'blessed' bonuses
[*]SimPlayers will be less likely to attack trivial mobs while in your group
[*]Combat log is now scrollable
[*]UI performance improvements
[*]Players can no longer cast spells while stunned / dazzled / sleeping, etc
[*]Delay between right clicking and item inspect window showing up is reduced
[*]SimPlayers far below your level will compliment your gear sometimes
[*]Adjusted some word parsing logic to better recognize context
[*]When entering a zone, NPC spawns are 'staggered' over about 4 seconds to prevent trying to perform all of the spawns in one frame (smoother zoning transitions)
[*]Mineral nodes can no longer be mined from infinite distance
[*]Brax's chains no longer gives an attack speed debuff
[*]Dying in a zone would erase all SimPlayer progress gained since entering that zone. This was not intended and is fixed.
[/list]

[u][b]Steam Deck: [/b][/u]
[list]
[*]Touchpad input will now unlock and show the mouse cursor without first using the DPAD. You may need to select the touchpad-as-mouse profile from your control options.
[/list]

Please report and be patient with any bugs! Erenshor is an ongoing work in progress and passing new development to the demo always comes with the risk of a new bug. 

Announcements for the Early Access release date are coming soon! Please spread the word about Erenshor, and if you haven't wishlisted the game yet, please consider doing it!

Thank you, as always, for playing Erenshor!
-Brian "Burgee"

notes.title: The gloom over Stowaway's Step Fades...
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Adventurers![/h1]

As of November 7th, Shivering Step is no longer available in the Erenshor Demo. I hope that this special Halloween event gave you a nice taste of things to come when Erenshor goes into Early Access release next year!

I want to extend a sincere [u][b]THANK YOU[/b][/u] to everyone who played the game during Steam Next Fest. If you blogged about it, shared it on a forum, made a youtube video, or otherwise spread the word - an extra [b]thank you[/b] to you.

[h3]Why is content being removed?[/h3]
Shivering Step was a [b]special event[/b] that was created without much attention paid to overall game balance. When players leave the demo island, the content that greets them on the mainland is geared for level 6-7 characters. 

Shivering Step is taking players to level 10+ and in those cases, the beginning of the actual game will be very trivialized and early game balance would be very skewed as a result. While it was hopefully fun for those who partook, it wasn't originally designed to be demo content.

All of the [b]Stowaway's Step[/b] and [b]Island Tomb [/b] content will remain available in the demo up to and beyond launch. 

Any players currently in Shivering Step will remain there until they leave the zone. This includes dying in the zone. Once you leave, the entrance to return will no longer exist.

[h1]Other changes this patch[/h1]

[b]Balance[/b]
-Int scaling changes on Damage Spells are live (does not affect DOTs at this time)
-Resonating spells get a 50% penalty to base damage
-NPC Damage Changes - most mobs will hit harder, bringing combat difficulty more in-line with the intended levels. Be careful!
-Instant cast spells like food, water, can't be interrupted by running anymore
-Instant cast spells can't resonate anymore
-Resist changes across the board - players should be overall a bit more resistant to magic in a lot of cases, more to come. 

[b]Other[/b]
-Fixed SimPlayer animations a bit, so they don't slide as much when moving
-Added some new attack animations to 1H sword and 2H swords just to give some variety (0 effect on damage)
-SimPlayers will hold more mana in reserve for healing
-The "Pull" button can be targeted at specific mobs. After the targeted mob is dead, pulling will continue with SimPlayers selecting targets. Pressing Stop allows you to target another specific mob for a pull by using the button again
-SimPlayers will no longer out-level you in the same party
-Casting spells gives every other hotkey a short 1/3rd second cooldown to allow variables to reset
-Items with spells now have cooldowns appropriate to whatever spell they're casting

[b]Bugs[/b]
-Fixed Null Reference Errors (2x)
-Bug and Typo fixes all over

[b]Steam Deck [/b]
-There have been reports of the mouse cursor not appearing properly on steam deck builds. This is being looked into. 
-A temporary workaround is to touch the screen to make the pointer appear, at which point you can use it normally until it disappears once you leave it idle. Repeat as necessary.

On the small island just off of the coast of Erenshor, something strange has happened. A quiet little crypt in the islands forest has begun to glow. A creature has emerged from its old wooden door and stands guard just outside. Players who gain entry will find a portal to Shivering Step - an alternate version of Stowaway's Step with its own story to tell.

To celebrate, we've created a new trailer: 
[previewyoutube=IGLcxOcyhLY;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


[h3]What's included in this update[/h3]

[list]
[*]Stowaway's Step has received a visual overhaul with new textures, more monsters, and color adjustments
[*]Shivering Step is open to explore! Content is intended for players level 6+ who have completed the main demo storyline.
[*]Over 25 new loot items to find and equip, 6 new bosses to defeat, and secrets to uncover.
[*]More SimPlayer interactivity - use /shout to find specific classes to group (e.g. "Need a druid for xp group!" or "Need DPS, anyone but Jethro, he sucks!"
[*]Dozens of small bug fixes, optimizations, QOL improvements, and other tweaks as requested by the Erenshor community
[*]As always, progress made in the demo will carry over to full release.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/ba4d20128ca8467025db7b43c496597e7e0182bb.png[/img]

[h3]What is Erenshor[/h3]

Harkening to beloved legacy MMOs of the 90s and early 2000s, like EverQuest and RuneScape, Erenshor recreates the experience of a typical MMORPG. However, instead of real players, would-be adventurers are surrounded by hundreds of “Simulated Players” who act as stand-ins for human gamers. Team up with these SimPlayers for raids, trading, and much more. As a single-player game, there are no time commitments—players can jump in and out whenever they like. The world continues to evolve in ‘real-time’ while real-life calls, but progress won’t be made until players hop back into the fray.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/a999988e6c2feb9f667463d308d68affa9dae882.png[/img]

[list]
[*] MMORPG Gameplay Without the Commitment: In Erenshor, players can revisit the feeling of MMORPG gameplay at their own pace and on their own time. Have to leave a raid early? Have to ditch your group for family time? Do it! Nobody will hold it against them, and they can pick up where they left off next time.

[*] Alone, but Never Lonely: Erenshor boasts a population of "SimPlayers" who will adventure right alongside you. They'll join your groups, insult your fashion, invite you to raids, and, most importantly - they'll progress on their own.

[*] A World Divided: Erenhor’s world is divided into separate 'zones.' Areas are unique to themselves and can be traversed at will - whether you’re equipped or not. Explore cities, dungeons, tombs, forests, beaches, forts, meadows, caves, and mountain ranges - a huge world to explore with secrets in every corner.

[*] Hundreds of Quests and NPCs to Discover: Though the adventure is a single-player experience, that doesn’t mean the world of Erenshor is a ghost town. Players will meet and interact with hundreds of in-world NPCs, many with quests to give or gossip to share.
[/list]
